purpose: Record the published algorithm settings considered for the P418 pore-scale CHT model comparison. These are numerical model settings, not physical pebble-bed parameters.
physical_parameter_rule: Operating conditions, material properties and boundary conditions remain those listed in literature_parameter_manifest.csv and hccb_p418_model_splits.json. No neural-network setting is allowed to alter them.

domain_specific_pinn_precedents.reported_method: A coordinate fully connected PINN maps (x,y) to (u,v,p,T), treats effective permeability and effective thermal conductivity as trainable quantities, uses tanh and Adam, and runs for 60000 epochs.

domain_specific_pinn_precedents.reported_loss_weights: Equation weights 1e3, 1 and 1e-19; overall PDE and data weights 1 and 1e4.
domain_specific_pinn_precedents.use_in_this_project: Direct domain precedent for using a PINN in HCCB packed-bed upscaling. It supports the choice of a coordinate-PINN baseline, but its unreported network settings are not invented or copied.

not_added_now.reason: Its per-axis separable computation is not a direct representation of the present unstructured conjugate fluid-solid regional graph.
A learned nonlinear latent encoder and decoder would overlap the DMDc/POD question while only twelve physical step trajectories are available.
A sinogram representation does not directly retain the present fluid-solid interface graph, unequal regional volumes and oriented finite-volume heat fluxes.

Porous-DeepONet is an important porous-structure solution-operator precedent, but its convolutional branch reads equal-spaced image-like structure fields. A separate branch-trunk formal model would require a common structured representation that the present unequal-volume fluid-solid regional graph does not provide, while only twelve physical step trajectories are available.

CNN and U-Net predictors are strong for voxel or equal-grid porous fields and large lattice-Boltzmann datasets. The present comparison instead retains unequal regional volumes, fluid-solid interfaces, oriented face mass and heat fluxes, and changing connectivity between pebble packings without voxel interpolation.

Finite-volume-constrained UNO-PINO is a relevant conservation precedent for two-dimensional steady heat conduction with discontinuous conductivity. The present task is three-dimensional transient fluid-solid conjugate heat transfer on irregular regional graphs; adding a formal UNO/FNO baseline would first require a common voxelized representation and enough physical trajectories to separate representation error from model error.

not_added_now.method: Graph-Physics temporal correction and local multi-node prediction
not_added_now.reason: The public implementation contains both extensions, but every checked training configuration at the locked commit disables them. The present comparison therefore retains the already implemented temporal Transformer and finite-volume regional losses instead of adding an unverified sixth formal architecture.

architecture_selection_boundary.revisit_condition: Reconsider additional pretrained or latent architectures only after multiple packings or hundreds of physical trajectories become available; do not enlarge the present comparison using the same twelve trajectories.

training_repeat_rule.reason: Three training seeds are used on the strict endpoint-pair-disjoint split to measure initialization and training variability without tripling every directional comparison.

steady_training_repeat_rule.reason: The main steady split is repeated with three independent initializations to measure neural-training variation. The four extrapolation splits retain the registered primary seed so that the complete five-split comparison is not tripled.
steady_training_repeat_rule.real_3d_software_check_scope: One training epoch on eight existing P418 3D fields. Same-seed predictions agree within float32 GPU accumulation differences, while different seeds produce much larger changes. These values verify the training procedure and are not model-accuracy results.

common_transient_energy_evaluation.reason: All temperature-field models are evaluated with the same transient fluid/solid energy operator. The primary comparison is the volume-weighted difference between the predicted regional operator and the OpenFOAM field projected onto the same regional geometry. Absolute regional residuals are reported only to expose projection error, while native OpenFOAM solver balances remain the conservation reference. CPU accumulation is retained because an actual 46089-node check gave exactly repeatable values for identical fields, whereas CUDA scatter accumulation showed small run-to-run differences.

latest_steady_software_test.scope: one training epoch on eight completed P418 OpenFOAM fields with six train, one validation and one independent-prediction condition; software-path check only
latest_steady_software_test.result: all five methods completed with finite state, mass-flow, energy-flow and engineering outputs; the one-epoch values are not model-accuracy evidence

latest_steady_small_condition_training_c.scope: 100 training epochs on eight completed P418 OpenFOAM fields with six train, one validation and one independent-test condition, followed by a 100-to-200-epoch graph-model extension; this checks small-sample behaviour before the formal 60-condition comparison
latest_steady_small_condition_training_c.result: the response surface gave the smallest independent-condition temperature errors with only six training conditions. Extending the graph model from 100 to 200 epochs reduced total state RMSE and solid-maximum-temperature error, but worsened outlet-temperature error and global energy balance. Therefore lower aggregate loss is not accepted as sufficient evidence of better engineering prediction; the formal comparison will report outlet temperature, solid hot spot, wall heat and energy balance separately across the 9, 18, 27 and 36-condition learning curve.
latest_steady_small_condition_training_c.engineering_metric_result: with six training conditions the response surface led five of seven independent engineering metrics, while Transolver led cooling-wall heat and the graph model led fluid-solid net heat transfer; no architecture led every physical quantity
latest_steady_small_condition_training_c.status: completed small-condition behaviour check; final model accuracy still waits for the formal 60-condition OpenFOAM dataset

architectures.name: PINO-paper coordinate PINN control
architectures.paper: Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Learning Partial Differential Equations
architectures.project_adaptation: The archived baseline maps (x,y,t) to three Navier-Stokes variables. The P418 control maps five literature operating conditions plus fixed regional coordinates, cell volume, fluid/solid type and boundary role to five CHT state channels. The six tanh layers, width 50, Glorot-normal initialization and Adam learning rate are retained. The common finite-volume mass and energy balance losses replace the Navier-Stokes residuals. Conservative face-output heads are shared with the graph and Transformer models. This is an adapted classical PINN control, not an exact reproduction of the 2024 HCCB inverse PINN paper.
architectures.status: architecture and optimizer are implemented from the archived source; one-epoch training and independent-condition prediction passed on eight actual P418 OpenFOAM fields with finite state/flux outputs; full 60-case training is pending

architectures.name: RIGNO-style regional graph operator
architectures.paper: RIGNO: A Graph-based Framework for Robust and Accurate Operator Learning for PDEs on Arbitrary Domains
architectures.project_adaptation: Regions follow native OpenFOAM finite-volume faces. Fluid and solid are aggregated separately and mapped fluid-solid faces remain a separate connection type. Official RIGNO uses one regional-node set with several connection ranges; the present finite-volume implementation instead provides an explicit aggregation hierarchy. The memory-bounded initial comparison uses the coarsest 46089-node graph and decodes the complete 1870064-cell field in chunks. It is therefore described as RIGNO-style rather than an exact RIGNO reproduction. The published processor_steps=12 remains the total message-passing depth and is never repeated at every level.

measured_compute_setting.reason: A two-condition CUDA batch used 19.76 GB on the actual 46089-node graph. One-condition microbatches with gradient accumulation reduced the peak to 10.02 GB while preserving one effective-batch update.

architectures.status: source-width forward and backward execution passed on the actual 46089-node graph; one-epoch CUDA training and independent-condition prediction passed on eight actual P418 OpenFOAM fields with effective batch two accumulated from one-condition microbatches; full training waits for the 60-case dataset

architectures.name: Transolver
architectures.role: Transformer comparison on unstructured regional nodes
architectures.paper: Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries
architectures.project_adaptation: Physics-Attention is applied only after finite-volume cells have been mapped to regional nodes; full attention over approximately 1.87 million original cells is not used. The official slice-attend-deslice sequence, eight heads, 32 slices, zero dropout and orthogonal slice projection are retained. On the project RTX 4000 Ada, the published effective batch size of eight is retained by accumulating gradients from one condition at a time; this changes memory scheduling rather than the network, loss or optimizer update.

measured_compute_setting.reason: A six-condition direct CUDA batch reached 19.22 GiB and failed while allocating the energy-face tensors; one-condition microbatches completed the same one-update smoke path.

architectures.name: Temporal Transformer trajectory operator
architectures.role: solver-relaxation acceleration and physical P418 endpoint step-response prediction for directly reported OpenFOAM observables
architectures.sizing_and_optimizer_source: Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries
architectures.project_adaptation: A standard temporal self-attention encoder has two explicitly separated uses. For solver acceleration, it maps each published P418 operating condition and steady-iteration coordinate to its complete OpenFOAM steady-solver relaxation trajectory through iteration 200. These labels are not physical time or physical start-up. For thermal dynamics, it maps the source and target P418 conditions plus physical time to a separate response after exactly one inlet-temperature, inlet-velocity or solid-heat-source step. Each step case starts from the converged steady-iteration-200 source fluid/solid temperatures and target U, p and p_rgh fields. The target hydrodynamic field is held fixed while the fluid and solid energy equations advance with an Euler time derivative. A 25 s representative calculation is used to determine whether the physical observation window needs extension; 300 s is only a candidate upper bound before that calculation. Complete curves, rather than individual time points, are separated between training, validation and testing. The dimensions and optimizer follow the Transolver comparison, but the attention is ordinary temporal self-attention rather than Transolver Physics-Attention. The outputs are outlet temperature, volume-average fluid/solid temperatures, oriented mass flow, inlet/outlet enthalpy flow, cooling-wall power and maximum solid temperature.
architectures.status: real OpenFOAM time-history export is implemented; a reduced one-epoch solver-relaxation smoke run passed on five completed curves; a 12-curve physical-step software test and complete-curve split test passed; formal source-sized training waits for the corresponding OpenFOAM histories

numerical_settings_reference.paper: MeshGraphNet-Transformer hybrid reported by Iparraguirre et al.
numerical_settings_reference.use_in_this_project: Only the listed layer counts, hidden path and attention dimensions are retained as a fixed, untuned implementation setting. The scientific architecture claim is based on the published component papers above, and this project is not presented as an exact reproduction of the preprint.

architectures.project_adaptation: The implemented model combines published mesh message passing, a RIGNO-style regional representation, Transolver Physics-Attention and an explicit temporal Transformer. Regional nodes and edges come from conservative OpenFOAM finite-volume aggregation. Each node receives its coordinates, log regional volume, fluid/solid type and the volume-weighted fractions of its fine cells adjacent to the inlet, outlet, cooling wall, symmetry boundary and fluid-solid interface. These are boundary-adjacency volume fractions, not boundary-area fractions, and are computed from the registered P425/P427 boundary layout and resolved mesh rather than fitted from the thermal histories. Velocity and pressure are copied from the converged target hydrodynamic state, and only temperature evolves. Because regional volume averaging does not commute with nonlinear finite-volume face fluxes, the PINN term minimizes the difference between the predicted regional transient-energy operator and the OpenFOAM reference projected onto the same regional geometry. Fluid and solid energy-residual differences are integrated with their finite-volume cell measures. Internal heat-flux differences are compared as heat-flux density with face-area integration, making the loss invariant when one geometric face is subdivided without changing its total area or heat flow. Absolute regional residuals for prediction and reference are reported as projection diagnostics and are not confused with native-mesh OpenFOAM closure. OpenFOAM reference edge heat flux is retained as an additional spatial-gradient target. The reference branch applies the spatial preprocessor to every time query. A separate factorized efficiency branch applies that preprocessor once to the fixed geometry, converged hydrodynamic state and step condition, then retains every declared time query, the temporal mixer, time-dependent local refinement and the same transient energy/flux losses. This is a project composition of published components, not an exact reproduction of any one paper.

fully_coupled_extension.method_source: MeshGraphNet and RIGNO edge-to-node message passing applied to finite-volume owner-neighbour connectivity
fully_coupled_extension.initial_active_boundary_face_flux_messag: inlet/outlet to owner; other boundary faces excluded
fully_coupled_extension.scope: The fully coupled branch advances velocity, pressure, temperature and oriented face mass flow. The stated message rules are numerical graph construction choices and introduce no new pebble-bed physical parameter.

architectures.status: The factorized branch completed forward execution, transient-energy and heat-flux evaluation, and backward propagation for the revised 56-snapshot plan on the actual 46089-node, 245848-edge regional graph. One update required 7.74 s and 18.99 GB on the RTX 4000 Ada, compared with 15.13 s and 19.64 GB for repeated spatial queries. The latter required expandable CUDA memory segments because it operates near the 20 GB device limit. The input geometry, topology, state targets, steady dataset and time plan were checked by SHA256 before execution. The batch is therefore restricted to one complete curve with gradient accumulation. Prediction accuracy still waits for the 12 OpenFOAM temperature-step histories.

architectures.name: Volume-weighted DMDc baseline
architectures.role: classical reduced-order baseline for regional thermal-step trajectories
architectures.venue: SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems 15 (2016) 142-161

source_settings.project_fit: midpoint reduced states and adjacent finite-difference time derivatives using the actual recorded time intervals
source_settings.project_time_integration: exact augmented linear-system matrix exponential over each recorded interval
source_settings.spatial_weighting: square root of regional volume normalized by mean regional volume

architectures.project_adaptation: The reduced state contains the volume-weighted regional fluid and solid temperatures. Because the 56 registered output times are nonuniform, adjacent reduced states are converted to midpoint states and physical-time derivatives to fit dz/dt=A z+B u. Prediction uses a matrix exponential over every original recorded interval, without interpolation to a uniform grid. The eight source/target operating quantities act as control inputs. Training curves alone determine the POD basis and DMDc matrices; the validation curves choose rank and the test curves are used only once for reporting.
architectures.status: completed as the non-neural regional-field baseline on the registered 12-trajectory physical-step dataset

architectures.project_adaptation: Only training-curve residuals between the physics-constrained graph-Transformer and OpenFOAM are decomposed. Formal execution requires the upstream predictor to be a completed physics-constrained run over all 12 disjoint thermal-step curves; software-smoke predictions are rejected. architectures.name: PDE-Refiner-style diffusion refinement
architectures.role: temperature-residual correction after a deterministic steady or transient CHT predictor
architectures.paper: PDE-Refiner: Achieving Accurate Long Rollouts with Neural PDE Solvers

partial_observation_source.paper: DiffusionPDE: Generative PDE-Solving under Partial Observation
partial_observation_source.use_boundary: Only the partial-observation problem formulation is transferred. Burgers-equation guidance weights are not copied to the pebble-bed thermal problem.

architectures.project_adaptation: Diffusion is restricted to the temperature residual after a deterministic CHT predictor. Formal execution requires the upstream predictor to be a completed physics-constrained run over all 12 disjoint thermal-step curves; software-smoke predictions are rejected. For the 12 thermal-step curves it combines regional Physics-Attention with temporal self-attention, imposes t=0 exactly and accepts only externally supplied measurement locations. Formal computed-residual comparisons use 32 fixed-seed samples and report 8/16/32 sample-count convergence, ensemble spread and descriptive interval coverage. The checkpoint is selected on validation curves before independent prediction. Deterministic, diffusion-refined and OpenFOAM reference temperatures are evaluated with the same transient fluid/solid energy equations. On independent test curves, every one of the 32 stochastic temperature samples is also inserted separately into those equations; the reported member distribution and joint-improvement fraction therefore do not rely only on the ensemble mean. Every held-out result is reported; it is described as a joint improvement only when solid-temperature RMSE decreases and the projection-aware energy residual does not increase. This held-out description is not used to select or update the model. The effective curve batch remains eight, but complete curves are processed one at a time and their volume-weighted gradients are accumulated before one optimizer and EMA update. CUDA activations use bfloat16 after a full-size backward test, while parameters and optimizer states remain float32. Model, EMA, optimizer, learning-rate schedule and random-generator states are atomically saved after every completed epoch so a matching run can continue after an interruption. These are seed-sensitivity results, not an experimentally calibrated posterior. It does not replace the finite-volume equations, alter any physical operating condition or create synthetic sensor positions.
architectures.status: Official PDE-Refiner scheduling, velocity targets, EMA training and reverse residual sampling are implemented for steady and temporal residuals. On the actual 46089-node graph, a 4096-node temporal block exhausted the 20 GB GPU during the revised 56-snapshot backward pass. Reducing only the temporal node block to 2048 retained all nodes and times and completed in 14.03 s with 18.75 GB peak memory and finite gradients. The geometry, topology and time-plan SHA256 values are stored with the result. Prediction accuracy still waits for the 12 OpenFOAM thermal-step histories.

comparison_rule: All architectures use the same 60 literature conditions, the same train/validation/test lists, the same train-only normalization and the same field and engineering metrics. Reduced smoke-test widths or layer counts may test software execution only and cannot be reported as the scientific comparison.
